subject: Next steps: tool-call & schema checklist for deterministic outputs
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Rajat Singh <rajat@stratopay.com>, Anika Bose <anika@stratopay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Quick summary + next steps (tool-calls & deterministic JSON needs)

Hi Rajat / Anika —

Thanks again for the time today. Short recap from our side so we’re aligned and can make the technical deep-dive productive. I kept this to the key pain points, your success criteria, and immediate next steps.

Pain points we heard
- Inconsistent JSON outputs from current generation layer: downstream services must parse predictable keys and types but current outputs require brittle parsing logic and lots of edge-case handling.
- Cost & latency: you’re seeing spiky per-token costs with current vendor; P50 latency is OK but p95 for short inference is too high for real-time flows.
- Orchestration complexity: multiple microservices call into LLM, and you want explicit function/tool-calling semantics to route actions (payments, KYC checks) deterministically.
- Compliance/data residency concerns for European customers — want clear deployment options and audit logs.

Current stack (as described)
- Node backend, Express services, Redis cache, internal orchestrator (go-based), vendor model access via standard REST.
- Some downstream parsers are brittle; roughly 6 services subscribe to generation outputs.

Success criteria (what would make this a win)
1) Deterministic structured outputs: Valid JSON that matches a provided JSON Schema 99%+ of the time on eval prompts (we’ll propose a schema-driving approach).
2) Latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens) in production region.
3) Cost: unit token cost reduction target (we discussed approx 30% improvement vs current vendor).
4) Operability: function/tool calling primitives so the LLM can return explicit, validated actions (tool_name + args) for downstream routing.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
- I’ll share a short checklist and two artifacts: (1) stratopay-prompt-sample.json (representative prompts + expected schema), (2) redwood-eval-checklist.md with deterministic-format success criteria.
- Schedule 90-minute technical deep-dive with Rishi (solutions), your infra lead, and our infra engineer to map integration patterns and run a small eval.
- I’ll open a HubSpot deal and share a temporary eval key for Dedicated/Hosted tests.

Attachments: [Attachment: stratopay-prompt-sample.json (JSON, 2.1KB)], [Attachment: redwood-eval-checklist.md (MD, 3.4KB)], [Attachment: SOW-template.pdf (PDF, 46KB)]

If this looks right, would you be available for the technical deep-dive next week Tues/Wed (May 2/3)? If those don’t work, propose two windows and I’ll coordinate with Rishi/Neha.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Rajat Singh <rajat@stratopay.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Anika Bose <anika@stratopay.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick summary + next steps (tool-calls & deterministic JSON needs)

Marcus — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Deterministic output: we don’t need 100% absolute determinism, but we need a contract-like guarantee for the keys used by downstream systems (types + required fields). Occasional filler text is OK as long as parsers never break.
- Tool-calls: the ideal shape is {"action":"charge_card","args":{...}} — we want recoverable failures (idempotency token + explicit error codes).
- Compliance: EU data must stay in eu-central for EU customers; can you confirm regional routing options and audit-log retention windows?

We’re happy to run a short eval as long as it doesn’t require infrastructure changes on our end. The evaluation should include 50 sample prompts and the schema-based pass/fail counts.

Regarding timing: Tue/Wed next week (June 1/2) would be better for our infra lead. Can you loop in Rishi and share the evaluation checklist before the call?

Thanks,
Rajat
Rajat Singh
